content.text: Anti-windup does not prove physical loop stability or optimality. The casebook gives an unreachable reference for a fixed interval and then lowers it. It compares model-integrated absolute error and final integrator values. Under the selected gains and synthetic plant, clamping improves its selected error metric. This is **not proof** that clamping always outperforms every other anti-windup design or that those gains are safe for an actual valve, heater or motor. Domain context: 07_pi_pid_saturation_and_anti_windup.md. A declared model is not a validated hardware controller.

content.text: Conditional integration can limit integrator buildup in a saturated model. MathWorks presents two documented anti-windup approaches—back-calculation and clamping—on a first-order process with actuator saturation and dead time. This Atlas implements only a **specific, discrete conditional integration** convention in a synthetic first-order, no-delay plant: `u=clip(kp*(r−y)+I, umin, umax)`. It freezes I when the proposed command is beyond a rail and the error would push it farther out; otherwise it integrates `I += ki Δt (r−y)`. The state update occurs after actuation via a zero-order-hold discrete model. The `none` mode integrates regardless of saturation. Domain context: 07_pi_pid_saturation_and_anti_windup.md. A declared model is not a validated hardware controller.
